verdict.rationale: Omarchy documents one-menu installs of current IDEs (VSCode, Cursor, Zed, Sublime, Helix, Neovim default) and development environments (Rails, Laravel, Node.js) with Mise for language versions. It also ships AI coding agents (OpenCode, Claude Code) and launchers for major agent CLIs. ML software beyond coding agents (CUDA, ML frameworks, GPU compute setup) is not documented; NVIDIA drivers are mentioned only in a gaming context. There is also no evidence that this Arch-based platform is a primary supported target for vendors' latest releases. missing for 10: documented AI/ML frameworks and GPU compute toolchain support, evidence of primary-platform vendor support for latest IDE and toolchain releases, independent hands-on corroboration of the dev-environment installs

support.subject: As a developer, I can use the latest IDEs, toolchains, and AI/ML software on a primary supported platform

citations.quote: Neovim is the default, with VSCode, Cursor, Zed, Sublime Text, Helix, Vim, and Emacs ready to install.
Install Ruby on Rails, Laravel, Node.js, and a long list of other development environments from the Omarchy menu. Mise handles language versions, so each project can use what it needs.
Omarchy ships with [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/) and [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) as the default agent harnesses for programmers.
Omarchy ships pre-wired lazy-loaded launchers for every major coding-agent CLI.
